ai.description: Hardwick’s Water Snake reaches 1 meter. It is greyish-brown with dark, irregular crossbands and a pale belly. Key features include a strongly keeled, dull-textured body and a broad, distinct head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Homalopsis hardwickii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged pale stripe running along the side of its head, passing through the eye.
ai.habitat: *Homalopsis hardwickii* inhabits coastal mangroves, tidal estuaries, and brackish marshes across the Indian subcontinent, typically at low elevations near sea level.
ai.behavior: Hardwick’s Water Snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting fish and crustaceans in murky, shallow aquatic habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Homalopsis hardwickii* is viviparous, producing litters of 6–20 young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with births recorded between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Homalopsis hardwickii occurs in coastal regions and estuaries of eastern India, specifically in West Bengal and Odisha, typically at low elevations near sea level.
